clue.text: Wagoner chopped pine in cold country

indicators.note: in tells us the shortened pine sits inside the country's name

parts.note: Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, so the word for pine loses its last letter

parts.note: to pine is to ache or yearn

explanation.surface: A wagon driver hacks at a pine tree somewhere chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' reads as the tree, but here it is the verb meaning to long for something.
explanation.definitionFit: A coachman drives a horse-drawn carriage, just as a wagoner drives a wagon: both are drivers of horse transport.

clue.text: Music speaker on hi-fi's second to none

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the speaker above what follows

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker

indicators.note: second picks out the second letter of the word hi-fi

parts.note: the word whose second letter is taken
nought, zero, read as the round letter

explanation.surface: A boast that a sound system's speaker is the best there is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second to none' looks like one phrase meaning best, but it splits into two pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale musical composition for voices and orchestra, usually on a sacred theme.

clue.text: Fan eating first of his endless selection boxes?

definitions.text: Fan eating first of his endless selection boxes?

indicators.note: boxes means the shortened selection word encloses the rest, as a box holds its contents
endless means the word for selection loses its final letter

parts.note: a selection is a choice

indicators.note: eating means the fan word takes in the letter that follows it

parts.note: to fan something is to cool it

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the word his

parts.note: the word whose opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone working steadily through boxes of assorted chocolates, one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: it builds the answer and describes it. A selection box is a box of assorted chocolates, a British Christmas staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocoholic is a person addicted to chocolate, exactly the fan who would eat box after box of assorted sweets.

clue.text: Potato salad that's highly unpromising as a rule

parts.note: murphy is an old slang word for a potato, from the Irish surname
slaw is short for coleslaw, a cabbage salad

explanation.surface: A potato salad that looks like a poor bet, generally speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a dish, but the answer is a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Murphy's law states that anything which can go wrong will, a pessimistic principle that expects the worst.

clue.text: Mind about old football team's foul

indicators.note: about means the word for mind goes around the other pieces

parts.note: nous is common sense or intelligence
a football side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Thinking back on a former football side's dirty tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul' reads as a football offence, but it is the adjective meaning nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Noxious means harmful or very unpleasant, as a foul smell or substance is.

clue.text: Shortly discontinue a series of columns

indicators.note: shortly means the word for discontinue is cut off before its end

parts.note: to stop something is to discontinue it
taken as written

explanation.surface: An order to end a row of newspaper columns soon.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered walkway in ancient Greek architecture, lined with a colonnade.

clue.text: Disaster if mounts on racecourse failing to finish

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second
in a down clue, mounts means the word climbs upwards, so it is read in reverse
failing to finish means the racecourse name drops its last letter

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: Catastrophe looms at the races if the horses' riders cannot complete the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounts' suggests horses, but it is the instruction to read the little word upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a complete failure, a humiliating disaster.

clue.text: So light, rucksack initially carried for several hours

indicators.note: carried means the word for so holds the letter inside it

parts.note: thus means so, therefore

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of rucksack

parts.note: the word whose opening letter is taken
daylight, the day as opposed to the night

explanation.surface: A hiker's backpack is so light it can be carried for hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' reads as describing the rucksack's weight, but it is the noun meaning daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: Thursday is one day of the week, a span made up of a number of hours.

clue.text: Override unfashionable fashion, so to speak

parts.note: something out is no longer in fashion

indicators.note: so to speak tells us the word is entered as it is pronounced, not as spelt

parts.note: a fashion is a manner or way of doing something

explanation.surface: Overruling a dated style, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' sits next to 'unfashionable' to suggest clothes, but here it means manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To outweigh something is to count for more than it, so overriding it in importance.

clue.text: Boast Virginia to be mother

parts.note: to be mother is the British idiom for pouring the tea, so it gives to pour

explanation.surface: Bragging that Virginia will be a mother.
explanation.walkthrough: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia. In Britain the person who pours the tea is said to 'be mother'.
explanation.definitionFit: To vapour is an old word meaning to talk emptily or brag, from the idea of hot air.

clue.text: Pair strive to upset right wing economist

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people try to topple a conservative economics expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A privatiser advocates selling state industries into private hands, a policy associated with the political right.

clue.text: Push crankshaft back holding spanner

indicators.note: back means the letters found are read from right to left
holding means the answer lies inside the words push crankshaft

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between push and crank

explanation.surface: Instructions for a mechanic to shove a crankshaft back in place with a wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanner' looks like the tool, but it means anything that spans a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch spans the space between two supports, so it is a spanner in the sense of something that bridges.

clue.text: Green and red flower that renews when brought in

parts.note: green means inexperienced, youthful
a flower is something that flows, and blood is the red liquid that flows

explanation.surface: Describes a red-and-green plant that blooms afresh when taken indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' reads as a bloom, but it means something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Young blood means new recruits who bring fresh energy, so a team brings them in to revitalise itself.

clue.text: Idol to have trouble containing horse in decline

parts.note: an idol is a false god

indicators.note: containing means the words for to have and trouble hold another letter between them

parts.note: to own is to have
ill means trouble or misfortune, as in ill fortune
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A fading pop star struggling to keep a racehorse as their career slides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' suggests an animal; here it is drug slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: To go downhill is an idiom for deteriorating, getting steadily worse.

clue.text: Agitated, as pal has large dogs

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize, meaning large

explanation.surface: A friend gets nervous because he owns some big dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lhasa apso is a small long-haired Tibetan breed, named after the city of Lhasa.

clue.text: Earth — extremely lumpy material

parts.note: the earth is the world

indicators.note: extremely picks out the outermost letters of lumpy

parts.note: the word whose two outer letters are taken

explanation.surface: Soil, made of a coarse, lumpy substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like a noun for stuff or fabric, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Worldly means concerned with physical, earthly things rather than the spiritual, which is one sense of material.

clue.text: Quivering "bye-bye" to Heather after endless grief

indicators.note: after places the shortened grief before the other pieces
endless means the word for grief loses its last letter

parts.note: woe is deep sorrow
B is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a bye, so two byes give BB
ling is a common name for heather

explanation.surface: Someone trembling as they say a tearful goodbye to a woman called Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored without the batter hitting the ball, written B. 'Heather' looks like a name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Wobbling means shaking or trembling unsteadily, as quivering does.

clue.text: I'm in no hurry to cover point in theory

indicators.note: to cover means the phrase surrounds the compass point

parts.note: said as I dally, since to dally is to take one's time
east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone taking their time over making a theoretical point.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideally means in a perfect world, how things would be in principle though perhaps not in practice.

clue.text: Investigate family involved in stolen goods ring

indicators.note: involved in means the family word is set inside the stolen goods word

parts.note: loot is stolen goods
kin are one's relatives
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Police probe a family caught up in a ring dealing in stolen property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' reads as a criminal gang, but here it is just a circle shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To look into something is an idiom for examining or inquiring into it.

clue.text: Aromatic tandoor stew

indicators.note: a stew mixes its ingredients up, so the letters are stirred together

explanation.surface: A fragrant dish cooked slowly in a clay oven.
explanation.walkthrough: A tandoor is the clay oven of Indian cooking; the stew is the instruction, not the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Odorant describes something that gives off a smell or scent, as an aromatic substance does.

clue.text: Leggy creature angry her husband has left her

parts.note: a black look is an angry one
a widow is a woman whose husband has died, departing this life

explanation.surface: A woman furious that her husband has walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left her' sounds like desertion, but a widow's husband has died.
explanation.definitionFit: The black widow is a venomous spider, and spiders are known for their eight long legs.

clue.text: County boundary overlooked by hill worker

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooked by puts the second piece above the first

parts.note: worker ants live in an anthill
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A county's border lies beneath the gaze of someone labouring on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hill worker' suggests a shepherd or farmer, but it is an insect from an anthill.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Ace spinner at peak

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A top spin bowler at the height of their powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a cricket bowler; here it is the child's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop means on the top of, so at the summit or peak.

clue.text: Pound cut in price in Herts town

parts.note: L stands for the pound, from the Latin libra
to etch is to cut lines into a surface
worth is value or price

explanation.surface: A discount in pounds sterling in a Hertfordshire shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is short for Hertfordshire, a county north of London. 'Cut in price' reads as a reduction but splits into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: Letchworth Garden City in Hertfordshire was the world's first garden city, founded in 1903.

clue.text: As dog goes, with ducks following

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nought, so two ducks are two Os

explanation.surface: A dog trotting along with ducks waddling after it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes' means says, as in 'the dog goes woof'.
explanation.definitionFit: Woof is the sound a dog makes, its bark written as a word.

clue.text: Ange, following gins, chucks goods off trolley

indicators.note: following puts the name after the drinks
chucks means throws out, so a G is removed from the word gins

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: G stands for good, and the plural goods says more than one G is thrown out, so Ange loses its G too

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman called Ange, after a few gins, throws the shopping out of her trolley.
explanation.walkthrough: Both gins and Ange lose their G. Off one's trolley is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Insane means mad, and off your trolley is a slang idiom for having lost your reason.

clue.text: Hammer a lid on, when he's departed

definitions.text: Hammer a lid on, when he's departed

indicators.note: to hammer something is to batter it out of shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: departed means the letters of he leave the word when

parts.note: taken as written
the word he, the 's being part of 'he has'

explanation.surface: Fixing the coffin lid once the man has died.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the answer and describes it: closing a coffin after a death.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail down is to fasten something firmly with nails, as an undertaker secures a coffin lid.

clue.text: Negotiations bound to dwell on work

parts.note: talks are formal negotiations
to bound is to leap, as a hop is

explanation.surface: Bargaining sessions that are sure to concentrate on employment issues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to', but bound is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk shop is an idiom for discussing your job, especially when socialising.
